concepts.label: NCE inside speech bubble
concepts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: iOS app-icon refinement preview.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET, the exact user-approved existing dark teal-green hand-drawn icon. This is NOT merely a loose style reference. Make a minimal precise edit to this image, keeping the original icon identity.
Preserve: the deep muted teal-green rounded-square background, the thin warm-white hand-ink open book in the lower half, the original many page strokes, book angle, proportions, curved book spine, white outer book contour, and the speech-bubble contour with its tail in the upper right. Preserve the original calm literary hand-drawn texture and spacing as closely as possible. Keep the surrounding narrow white presentation margin. Output a single high-resolution square preview of the edited icon, with no heading, no alternate variants, no phone mockup or extra artwork.
Required added text: exact uppercase Latin letters "NCE", spelled N C E, clean, strong, correctly rendered and legible. Refined medium-bold editorial serif typography, warm white to match the existing illustration. Do NOT make a badge, sticker, separate colored plaque or outlined rectangle around the lettering. No Chinese or other text, no numerals, no four-book pile, no new illustrations, no colors besides the original green and white. Do not change this into a completely different flat book logo, and do not erase, redraw or simplify the approved illustration. No gradients, plastic 3D, gloss, shadows, ornamentation, watermark or publisher logo.
Change only the THREE SMALL WHITE DOTS inside the upper-right speech bubble: replace those dots with the word "NCE". Center NCE inside the existing speech bubble. The lettering fills about 72 percent of the bubble interior width, with adequate clear padding from the white contour. The existing bubble outline and its tail remain intact, and all original book artwork and other positions remain unchanged. Do not add any other NCE elsewhere. This should look like the book is speaking its own app name. Make the letters visually strong enough to read within the bubble, but do not enlarge the bubble or turn the word into an oversized heading.
